Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Subject: Post-demo recap & proposed next steps

Claire — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Highlights from the call:
- Your top goals: 1) accurate long-form summarization of policy documents (low hallucination), 2) <120ms median latency for interactive agent flows, 3) predictable per-request cost for scaling to ~25M tokens/month.
- Concern raised: hallucination on RARE legal clauses and PDF->extraction edge cases.

Suggested immediate next steps:
1) Pilot eval (2-week) using the prompt pack attached (lumos_prompt_set_v2.json) — includes representative policy excerpts + negative tests.
2) Run the three candidate models below on your eval set; we’ll supply a small benchmark harness and latency trace.
3) Configure prefix KV caching for repeated doc references and a canary rollout (5% traffic) for production validation.

Attachments I've included: lumos_prompt_set_v2.json (prompt + eval sets), lumos_benchmarks_20270928.pdf (our internal perf primer), demo_recording_20270929.mp4 (call recording). Also sharing our bench and run logs here: https://redwood.in/bench/lumosai/20270928

Tentative timeline if you greenlight:
- This week: sign-off on evaluation scope and provide 50-100 sample docs.
- Next week: Redwood runs evals / delivers scorecard + latency traces.
- Week 3: pilot pilot plan + pricing for a 3-month pilot.

Ben and I will coordinate the evaluation harness and cost estimates. Please let us know any constraints (data residency, IP terms) we should surface to legal early.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0194

Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 09:45:00 -0700
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Claire Hu <claire@lumos.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & proposed next steps — candidate models + cost/latency/quality tradeoffs

Claire — answers below plus a recommended shortlist and concrete bench numbers from our private runs (attached). TL;DR: two-tier pilot approach — a higher-precision float model for gold-paths and a quantized lower-cost fallback for scale.

Hallucination metrics we report in the scorecard:
- Hallucination rate (false-assertion / total responses) computed against a human-labeled truth set.
- Fact-error examples with classification (omission, fabrication, misattribution).
- Precision@k on entity extract / citation anchors for legal clauses.

Candidate shortlist (recommended ordering for the pilot):
1) Redwood-3-xl (fp16) — Best quality, strongest on long-context summarization and citations.
   - Median latency (interactive, 1-2 request batch): ~110ms @ p3/rt-optimized nodes
   - Cost: ~ $85 / 1M tokens (hosted pricing estimate for pilot volumes)
   - Notes: highest pass-rate on hallucination tests in our lab (hallucination rate ~1.8% on Lumos eval set).
2) Redwood-2-large-q4f — Quantized variant that balances quality and cost; good baseline for production A/B.
   - Median latency: ~85ms (improved throughput due to quant path)
   - Cost: ~ $34 / 1M tokens
   - Notes: Hallucination rate ~3.4% on the same eval; better throughput and predictable tail latency.
3) OpenSuite-7b-quant (community) — lowest $/token, useful as a fallback for non-critical flows.
   - Median latency: ~70ms
   - Cost: ~ $12 / 1M tokens
   - Notes: quality gap vs Redwood-3-xl on citation tasks; recommended only as a controlled fallback.

Recommended pilot configuration:
- Phase A (2 weeks): run Redwood-3-xl + Redwood-2-large-q4f across the prompt set (attached). Deliver: scorecard with hallucination examples, latency distributions, and per-prompt token cost.
- Phase B (canary): route 5% real traffic to the chosen model + data capture for regression alerts. We’ll hook tracing and automatic rollback if hallucination rate spikes >2x baseline.

Operational notes we’ll implement for the pilot:
- KV caching for repeated context (expected token cost reduction 12-18% for your workflows).
- Per-route quantization policies (keep gold-paths on fp16).
- Regression alerting tied to prompt-level metrics (precision drop, latency SLO breaches).

Benchmarks and artifacts: 
- Full run logs + perf CSV: https://redwood.in/bench/lumosai/20270928
- Prompt pack (attached): lumos_prompt_set_v2.json — includes positive/negative cases and edge-case PDFs.
- Summary PDF: lumos_benchmarks_20270928.pdf (attached).

Ballpark economics (pilot scale, monthly avg for 10M tokens):
- Redwood-3-xl: ~$850/month
- Redwood-2-large-q4f: ~$340/month
- OpenSuite-7b-quant: ~$120/month

Next asks from you to get started:
1) Confirm evaluation scope (we can adopt the attached prompt set or you can swap in your 50 examples).
2) Any must-have compliance requirements (e.g., specific KMS, data retention windows).
3) Greenlight for pilot SOW so procurement/legal can prepare a short 3-month trial.

If helpful I can also run a short annotated example run (5 prompts) and share the human-labeled scorecard by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
